JEE Main Mathematics, Unit 11: Three Dimensional Geometry: Teacher bank

140 questions · four options, one correct · marking +4 / −1 / 0. Difficulty labels are editorial estimates. Unless a question says otherwise: log without a base and loge denote the natural logarithm; arguments of complex numbers are principal values in (−π, π]; inverse trigonometric functions take principal values. Syllabus basis: NTA JEE Main 2026.

Includes keys, worked solutions, targeted misconceptions and numerical-answer forms.

JEE-MATH-U11-001 · Unit 11: Three Dimensional Geometry · Coordinates of a point in space · Easy · Class XI
The distance between the points P(1,2,−3) and Q(3,−1,3) is
  1. (A)7
  2. (B)17​
  3. (C)49
  4. (D)11
Answer and solution

Answer: (A) 7

The differences of coordinates are 2,−3,6, so PQ=4+9+36​=49​=7.

Targets: Adding coordinates or absolute differences instead of using the distance formula.
Difficulty: Direct use of the distance formula in one step.
Family: U11-A-distance-basic · Check: MACHINE_RECOMPUTED; BLIND_RESOLVED; EDITORIAL_AUDITED; ERRATA_RECOMPUTED; ERRATA_AUDITED

Numerical-answer form: The distance between the points P(1,2,−3) and Q(3,−1,3) is Answer: 7
JEE-MATH-U11-002 · Unit 11: Three Dimensional Geometry · Coordinates of a point in space · Easy · Class XI
The distance of the point P(3,−4,12) from the y-axis is
  1. (A)13
  2. (B)317​
  3. (C)5
  4. (D)4
Answer and solution

Answer: (B) 317​

The foot of the perpendicular from P to the y-axis is (0,−4,0), so the distance is x2+z2​=9+144​=153​=317​.

Targets: Using the coordinate itself, or the wrong pair of coordinates, for the distance from an axis.
Difficulty: One idea: the distance from the y-axis uses the other two coordinates.
Family: U11-A-distance-axis, ALIAS-ERR-U11-C-01 · Check: MACHINE_RECOMPUTED; BLIND_RESOLVED; EDITORIAL_AUDITED; ERRATA_RECOMPUTED; ERRATA_AUDITED

JEE-MATH-U11-003 · Unit 11: Three Dimensional Geometry · Coordinates of a point in space · Easy · Class XI
The point which divides the line segment joining P(2,−3,4) and Q(8,0,10) internally in the ratio 1:2 (that is, PX:XQ=1:2) is
  1. (A)(6,−1,8)
  2. (B)(4,−2,6)
  3. (C)(5,−23​,7)
  4. (D)(−4,−6,−2)
Answer and solution

Answer: (B) (4,−2,6)

X=31⋅Q+2⋅P​=(38+4​,30−6​,310+8​)=(4,−2,6).

Targets: Placing the ratio weights on the wrong endpoints.
Difficulty: Single application of the section formula.

JEE-MATH-U11-004 · Unit 11: Three Dimensional Geometry · Coordinates of a point in space · Easy · Class XI
Two vertices of a triangle are P(2,−1,4) and Q(3,5,−2), and its centroid is G(1,2,1). The third vertex R is
  1. (A)(2,−2,−1)
  2. (B)(−2,2,1)
  3. (C)(−4,−2,−1)
  4. (D)(−3,0,0)
Answer and solution

Answer: (B) (−2,2,1)

Since G=3P+Q+R​, R=3G−P−Q=(3−2−3, 6+1−5, 3−4+2)=(−2,2,1).

Targets: Forgetting the factor 3 in the centroid formula when solving for a vertex.
Difficulty: One rearrangement of the centroid formula.

JEE-MATH-U11-005 · Unit 11: Three Dimensional Geometry · Direction ratios and direction cosines · Easy · Class XII
A line has direction ratios 2,−1,2 and makes an obtuse angle with the positive direction of the x-axis. Its direction cosines are
  1. (A)−92​,91​,−92​
  2. (B)−52​,51​,−52​
  3. (C)32​,−31​,32​
  4. (D)−32​,31​,−32​
Answer and solution

Answer: (D) −32​,31​,−32​

22+12+22​=3, so the direction cosines are ±(32​,−31​,32​). An obtuse angle with the x-axis needs l<0, so take the negative sign: −32​,31​,−32​.

Targets: Ignoring the sign choice fixed by the angle condition.
Difficulty: Normalise once and choose the sign.
Family: U11-A-dc-from-dr · Check: MACHINE_RECOMPUTED; BLIND_RESOLVED; EDITORIAL_AUDITED; ERRATA_RECOMPUTED; ERRATA_AUDITED

JEE-MATH-U11-006 · Unit 11: Three Dimensional Geometry · Direction ratios and direction cosines · Easy · Class XII
A line makes angles of 45∘ and 60∘ with the positive x-axis and positive y-axis respectively, and an acute angle γ with the positive z-axis. Then γ equals
  1. (A)45∘
  2. (B)60∘
  3. (C)30∘
  4. (D)75∘
Answer and solution

Answer: (B) 60∘

cos245∘+cos260∘+cos2γ=1 gives cos2γ=1−21​−41​=41​. As γ is acute, cosγ=21​ and γ=60∘.

Targets: Treating the angles with the axes as summing to 180∘ instead of using l2+m2+n2=1.
Difficulty: One identity l2+m2+n2=1 applied once.
Family: U11-A-axes-angles · Check: MACHINE_RECOMPUTED; BLIND_RESOLVED; EDITORIAL_AUDITED; ERRATA_RECOMPUTED; ERRATA_AUDITED

Numerical-answer form: A line makes angles of 45∘ and 60∘ with the positive x-axis and positive y-axis respectively, and an acute angle γ with the positive z-axis. The value of γ in degrees is Answer: 60
JEE-MATH-U11-007 · Unit 11: Three Dimensional Geometry · Direction ratios and direction cosines · Easy · Class XII
Which of the following triples can be the direction cosines of a line?
  1. (A)21​,21​,21​
  2. (B)72​,73​,76​
  3. (C)2​1​,2​1​,21​
  4. (D)31​,31​,31​
Answer and solution

Answer: (B) 72​,73​,76​

Direction cosines must satisfy l2+m2+n2=1. For 72​,73​,76​ the sum of squares is 494+9+36​=1; the other triples give 43​, 31​ and 45​.

Targets: Using l+m+n=1 as the defining condition.
Difficulty: Recall of one condition, checked on four triples.
Family: U11-A-dc-validity · Check: MACHINE_RECOMPUTED; BLIND_RESOLVED; EDITORIAL_AUDITED; ERRATA_RECOMPUTED; ERRATA_AUDITED

  1. (A)cos−1(94​)

  3. (C)cos−1(814​)
  4. (D)cos−1(98​)
Answer and solution

Answer: (A) cos−1(94​)

cosθ=9​9​∣1⋅2+2⋅2+2⋅(−1)∣​=94​, so θ=cos−1(94​).

JEE-MATH-U11-009 · Unit 11: Three Dimensional Geometry · Coordinates of a point in space · Easy · Class XI
If the points P(1,2,3), Q(3,k,7) and R(5,8,11) are collinear, then k equals
  1. (A)8
  2. (B)14
  3. (C)3
  4. (D)5
Answer and solution

Answer: (D) 5

PQ​=(2,k−2,4) and PR=(4,6,8) must be proportional. The ratio is 42​=84​=21​, so k−2=3 and k=5.

Targets: Mishandling the proportionality constant between direction ratios.
Difficulty: One proportionality condition.

JEE-MATH-U11-010 · Unit 11: Three Dimensional Geometry · Coordinates of a point in space · Easy · Class XI
The yz-plane divides the line segment joining P(−2,4,7) and Q(3,−5,8) in the ratio
  1. (A)2:3 internally
  2. (B)7:8 externally
  3. (C)3:2 internally
  4. (D)4:5 internally
Answer and solution

Answer: (A) 2:3 internally

Let the point be k+1kQ+P​. On the yz-plane, x=0: k+13k−2​=0, so k=32​. The ratio is 2:3, and it is internal since k>0.

Targets: Setting the wrong coordinate to zero for a given coordinate plane.

JEE-MATH-U11-012 · Unit 11: Three Dimensional Geometry · Coordinates of a point in space · Easy · Class XI

  1. (A)8
  2. (B)5
  3. (C)7
  4. (D)6
Answer and solution

Answer: (C) 7

(a−1)2+32+(−2)2=49, so (a−1)2=36 and a=7 or a=−5. With a>0, a=7.

  1. (A)(3,3,−4)

JEE-MATH-U11-014 · Unit 11: Three Dimensional Geometry · Coordinates of a point in space · Easy · Class XI
Statement I: The points (1,2,3), (2,3,4) and (4,5,6) are collinear. Statement II: The points (1,−1,2), (2,1,3) and (4,5,6) are collinear. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer.
  1. (A)Statement I is true but Statement II is false
  2. (B)Both Statement I and Statement II are false
  3. (C)Both Statement I and Statement II are true
  4. (D)Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Answer and solution

Answer: (A) Statement I is true but Statement II is false

Statement I: the differences from the first point are (1,1,1) and (3,3,3), which are proportional, so the points are collinear. Statement II: the differences are (1,2,1) and (3,6,4); since 14​=3, they are not proportional, so the points are not collinear.

Targets: Checking proportionality on only some of the components.
Difficulty: Two direct proportionality checks.
Family: U11-A-st-collinear · Check: MACHINE_RECOMPUTED; BLIND_RESOLVED; EDITORIAL_AUDITED; ERRATA_RECOMPUTED; ERRATA_AUDITED

JEE-MATH-U11-015 · Unit 11: Three Dimensional Geometry · Direction ratios and direction cosines · Medium · Class XII
A line makes angles α,β,γ with the positive coordinate axes. Statement I: sin2α+sin2β+sin2γ=2. Statement II: cos2α+cos2β+cos2γ=−1. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer.
  1. (A)Statement I is false but Statement II is true
  2. (B)Both Statement I and Statement II are false
  3. (C)Both Statement I and Statement II are true
  4. (D)Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Answer and solution

Answer: (C) Both Statement I and Statement II are true

With cos2α+cos2β+cos2γ=1: ∑sin2α=3−1=2, and ∑cos2α=∑(2cos2α−1)=2−3=−1. Both statements are true.

Targets: Assuming the sine squares also add to 1, or misremembering the double-angle formula.
Difficulty: Two identities, each derived from l2+m2+n2=1.
Family: U11-A-st-axes-identity · Check: MACHINE_RECOMPUTED; BLIND_RESOLVED; EDITORIAL_AUDITED; ERRATA_RECOMPUTED; ERRATA_AUDITED

JEE-MATH-U11-016 · Unit 11: Three Dimensional Geometry · Direction ratios and direction cosines · Medium · Class XII
A line makes an angle θ with each of the positive x- and y-axes and an angle ϕ with the positive z-axis. If sin2θ=3sin2ϕ, then cos2θ equals
  1. (A)76​
  2. (B)41​
  3. (C)74​
  4. (D)71​
Answer and solution

Answer: (D) 71​

2cos2θ+cos2ϕ=1 gives sin2ϕ=1−cos2ϕ=2cos2θ. Then 1−cos2θ=3⋅2cos2θ, so 7cos2θ=1 and cos2θ=71​.

Targets: Counting the repeated angle once in l2+m2+n2=1.
Difficulty: Two relations combined; the repeated angle must be counted twice.

JEE-MATH-U11-017 · Unit 11: Three Dimensional Geometry · Direction ratios and direction cosines · Medium · Class XII
Direction ratios of a line perpendicular to both the lines with direction ratios 1,2,3 and 2,−1,1 are proportional to
  1. (A)1,−1,−1
  2. (B)2,−2,3
  3. (C)1,1,−1
  4. (D)3,1,4
Answer and solution

Answer: (C) 1,1,−1

Solve a+2b+3c=0 and 2a−b+c=0: the solution is proportional to (2⋅1−3⋅(−1), 3⋅2−1⋅1, 1⋅(−1)−2⋅2)=(5,5,−5), that is, to 1,1,−1. Check: 1+2−3=0 and 2−1−1=0.

Difficulty: Two perpendicularity conditions solved together.

JEE-MATH-U11-018 · Unit 11: Three Dimensional Geometry · Angle between two lines · Medium · Class XII
The lines with direction ratios k,2,−3 and 2k,k,4 are perpendicular. The sum of all possible values of k is
  1. (A)−6
  2. (B)1
  3. (C)6
  4. (D)−1
Answer and solution

Answer: (D) −1

k⋅2k+2⋅k+(−3)⋅4=0 gives 2k2+2k−12=0, that is, k2+k−6=0, so k=2 or k=−3. The sum is −1.

Targets: Sign error in the sum of roots −ab​.
Difficulty: Perpendicularity condition leads to a quadratic; then Vieta.

JEE-MATH-U11-019 · Unit 11: Three Dimensional Geometry · Angle between two lines · Medium · Class XII
If the lines with direction ratios 2,a,3 and b,−2,6 are parallel, then a+b equals
  1. (A)−3
  2. (B)0
  3. (C)3
  4. (D)5
Answer and solution

Answer: (C) 3

Parallel lines have proportional direction ratios: b2​=−2a​=63​=21​. So b=4 and a=−1, and a+b=3.

Targets: Inverting the ratio between the two sets of direction ratios.
Difficulty: Two unknowns from one proportionality chain.

JEE-MATH-U11-020 · Unit 11: Three Dimensional Geometry · Coordinates of a point in space · Medium · Class XI
The triangle with vertices P(1,0,2), Q(3,2,3) and R(3,−1,0) is
  1. (A)isosceles but not right-angled
  2. (B)equilateral
  3. (C)right-angled but not isosceles
  4. (D)right-angled and isosceles
Answer and solution

Answer: (D) right-angled and isosceles

PQ2=4+4+1=9, PR2=4+1+4=9, QR2=0+9+9=18. So PQ=PR and PQ2+PR2=QR2: the triangle is right-angled at P and isosceles.

Targets: Stopping after two sides, or not testing Pythagoras.
Difficulty: Three distances and two tests combined.
Family: U11-A-triangle-type · Check: MACHINE_RECOMPUTED; BLIND_RESOLVED; EDITORIAL_AUDITED; ERRATA_RECOMPUTED; ERRATA_AUDITED

JEE-MATH-U11-021 · Unit 11: Three Dimensional Geometry · Coordinates of a point in space · Medium · Class XI
The area of the triangle with vertices P(1,2,3), Q(2,3,1) and R(3,1,2) is
  1. (A)33​
  2. (B)432​​
  3. (C)233​​
  4. (D)3
Answer and solution

Answer: (C) 233​​

PQ2=1+1+4=6, QR2=1+4+1=6, RP2=4+1+1=6, so the triangle is equilateral with side 6​. Area =43​​⋅6=233​​.

JEE-MATH-U11-022 · Unit 11: Three Dimensional Geometry · Angle between two lines · Medium · Class XII

JEE-MATH-U11-023 · Unit 11: Three Dimensional Geometry · Direction ratios and direction cosines · Medium · Class XII
The projections of a line segment on the x-, y- and z-axes are 4, −3 and 12 respectively. The projection of this segment on the line joining R(1,0,2) to S(3,−2,3) is
  1. (A)26
  2. (B)926​
  3. (C)326​
  4. (D)314​
Answer and solution

Answer: (C) 326​

The segment is the vector (4,−3,12). The line RS has direction ratios 2,−2,1 and direction cosines 32​,−32​,31​. Projection =4⋅32​+(−3)(−32​)+12⋅31​=38+6+12​=326​.

JEE-MATH-U11-026 · Unit 11: Three Dimensional Geometry · Coordinates of a point in space · Medium · Class XI
In triangle PQR, the midpoints of QR, RP and PQ are K(1,2,−3), L(3,0,1) and M(−1,1,−4) respectively. The vertex P is

L+M=2R+P​+2P+Q​=P+2Q+R​=P+K. So P=L+M−K=(3−1−1, 0+1−2, 1−4+3)=(1,−1,0).

Answer: (C) (3,−3,6)

JEE-MATH-U11-028 · Unit 11: Three Dimensional Geometry · Direction ratios and direction cosines · Medium · Class XII
Statement I: There is a line that makes angles 30∘, 45∘ and 60∘ with the positive x-, y- and z-axes respectively. Statement II: There is a line that makes angles 45∘, 45∘ and 90∘ with the positive x-, y- and z-axes respectively. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer.
  1. (A)Both Statement I and Statement II are true
  2. (B)Statement I is true but Statement II is false
  3. (C)Statement I is false but Statement II is true
  4. (D)Both Statement I and Statement II are false

Answer: (C) Statement I is false but Statement II is true

Answer: (C) a rhombus but not a square

The midpoints of PR and QS are both (1,1,1), so PQRS is a parallelogram. PQ2=1+1+9=11 and QR2=9+1+1=11, so adjacent sides are equal: a rhombus. The diagonals are PR=16+4+16​=6 and QS=4+0+4​=22​, which are unequal, so it is not a square.

The nearest point is the foot of the perpendicular. A point of the line is (λ,2λ,2λ), and (λ−4)+2(2λ−3)+2(2λ−4)=9λ−18=0 gives λ=2. The point is (2,4,4), so α+β+γ=10.

Answer: (B) (3,1,4)

Let X=(1+λ,−1+λ,2+λ). Then XP2=(2+λ)2+λ2+(1+λ)2 and XQ2=(λ−2)2+λ2+(3+λ)2. Expanding, 3λ2+6λ+5=3λ2+2λ+13, i.e. 4λ=8, so λ=2 and X=(3,1,4).

  1. (A)−3x−1​=6y+1​=4z−2​

Answer and solution

Answer: (D) −1x−1​=4y+1​=3z−2​

Equating x and y: 3+λ=5+4μ and 3+2λ=−5−4μ; adding gives λ=−2, so μ=−1, and the z-coordinates agree (6−4=2=0+2). So X=(1,−1,2). Answer: (B) 6

The foot is F(λ,λ,λ) with (λ−k)+(λ−2)+(λ−1)=0, so λ=3k+3​. The image is 2F−P, whose x-coordinate is 32(k+3)​−k. Setting it to 0: 2k+6=3k, so k=6 (the image is (0,4,5)).

Answer: (C) −1x−2​=5y−1​=3z−1​

Every point of the x-axis has y=0 and z=0. A general point of the line is (1+2t, k+3t, −2+t). Putting z=0 gives t=2, and then y=k+6=0 gives k=−6. The common point is (5,0,0), so for k=−6 the line does meet the x-axis.

A rectangular box has one vertex at the origin O and edges of lengths 1,2,3 along the positive x-, y- and z-axes. The shortest distance between the diagonal of the bottom face joining O to (1,2,0) and the diagonal of the face y=0 joining (0,0,3) to (1,0,0) is
  1. (A)532​​

Answer: (B) 76​

The first diagonal is r=λ(1,2,0) and the second is r=(0,0,3)+μ(1,0,−3). They share no vertex and are not parallel. Then (1,2,0)×(1,0,−3)=(−6,3,−2), of magnitude 36+9+4​=7. With a2​−a1​=(0,0,3), the dot product is −6. So the shortest distance is 76​.

L1​ has direction (3,−1,2)−(1,0,2)=(2,−1,0) and L2​ has direction (0,1,−1). A common perpendicular is along (2,−1,0)×(0,1,−1)=((−1)(−1)−0⋅1, 0⋅0−2(−1), 2⋅1−(−1)⋅0)=(1,2,2), of magnitude 3. Since γ is acute, the direction cosines are 31​,32​,32​ (not their negatives), so the sum is 35​.

  1. (A)34
  2. (B)39
  3. (C)106
  4. (D)25
Answer and solution

Answer: (A) 34

The directions (1,2,2) and (2,−2,1) have dot product 2−4+2=0, so the lines are perpendicular. Their cross product is (6,3,−6), of magnitude 9, and with a2​−a1​=(−2,1,3) the dot product is −12+3−18=−27, so PQ=3. Now ST=SP+PQ​+QT​, where SP lies along L1​, QT​ along L2​, and PQ​ is perpendicular to both; since L1​⊥L2​ as well, the three vectors are mutually perpendicular. Hence ST2=32+32+42=34, whichever side of P and Q the points S and T lie.

JEE-MATH-U11-134 · Unit 11: Three Dimensional Geometry · Condition for intersection of two lines · Difficult · Class XII
The set of all real values of k for which the lines kx−1​=1y+1​=2z−2​ and 2x−1​=1y​=kz−3​ intersect is
  1. (A){−1,2}
  2. (B){−1}
  3. (C){1,−2}
  4. (D){2}
Answer and solution

Answer: (B) {−1}

With a2​−a1​=(0,1,1), the coplanarity condition is ​0k2​111​12k​​=−(k2−4)+(k−2)=−(k−2)(k+1)=0, so k=2 or k=−1. For k=2 both directions are (2,1,2), and (0,1,1) is not along it, so the lines are parallel and distinct, not intersecting. For k=−1 the directions (−1,1,2) and (2,1,−1) are not parallel, so the lines intersect. The set is {−1}.

Let λ,k∈R. The lines 2x−1​=1y−λ​=−2z+1​ and −4x−3​=ky+1​=4z−1​ are coplanar but do not intersect, and the distance between them is 4. Then the product of all possible values of λ is
  1. (A)−8
  2. (B)−11
  3. (C)−7
  4. (D)8
Answer and solution

Answer: (A) −8

Two coplanar lines that do not meet must be parallel, so (−4,k,4) is proportional to (2,1,−2), giving k=−2. Take b=(2,1,−2), ∣b∣=3, and a2​−a1​=(2,−1−λ,2); put u=λ+1. Then ∣a2​−a1​∣2=8+u2 and (a2​−a1​)⋅b=4−u−4=−u, so d2=8+u2−9u2​=8+98u2​. Setting d2=16 gives u2=9, so λ=2 or λ=−4; for both the lines are distinct parallel lines, as required. The product is −8.
